To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the excise tax that maximizes revenue is the one that results in an excise tax‐price ratio equal to the inverse of the price elasticity of demand.

over‐shifting is a structural phenomenon, that it is a function of the price elasticity of demand, that over‐shifter excise taxes are revenue maximizing, and that over‐shifted excise taxes can be reduced by increasing the price elasticity of supply.

the price elasticity of demand, the degree of over‐shifting, and the revenue‐maximising tax‐price ratio are all functions of the constant elasticity demand parameter, the number of firms, the tax elasticity, and the number of goods.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
excise taxes are a very blunt tool to control demand for a product.
the price elasticity of demand is not the sole determinant of over‐shifting, but that it is a necessary component.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
excise tax revenue is maximized when the tax‐price ratio is equal to the price elasticity of demand.
the price elasticity of demand is a critical parameter for excise tax policy, and it is important to consider the demand function and the market structure when estimating the elasticity.
the excise tax should be set to maximize revenue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
excise taxes should be set high enough to maximize tax revenues, but not so high as to discourage consumption and reduce tax revenues.
the price elasticity of demand for a particular good is not the only determinant of over‐shifting.
the revenue‐maximising excise tax‐price ratio is lower than that of a proportional tax, and that it is lower the more inelastic the demand for the good is.
